question: Should Claw mission control become a core OpenClaw surface now, and if so what storage/API boundary must it use before merge?
rationale: The PR adds a large new product surface plus config, Gateway protocol, UI, docs, workflow, browser, and persisted-state behavior; source review can identify blockers, but maintainers must decide whether this belongs in core and what permanent storage/API contract is acceptable.

options.title: Sponsor after blockers fixed
options.body: Keep the PR open only if maintainers want Claw in core and require SQLite-backed state, mission-id containment, HTTP/1 dispatcher preservation, a clean rebase, and real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Split into smaller PRs
options.body: Ask for separate browser/runtime hardening, docs/spec, and mission-control API PRs so each boundary can be reviewed and proven independently.

options.title: Pause or close direction
options.body: If Claw is not ready for core sponsorship, close or pause this broad branch and invite a narrower maintainer-owned proposal later.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after blockers fixed
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open only if maintainers want Claw in core and require SQLite-backed state, mission-id containment, HTTP/1 dispatcher preservation, a clean rebase, and real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: @steipete is the strongest history-backed owner for the storage policy, current guarded-network implementation, and adjacent UI/runtime surfaces implicated by this PR.
